- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If forecast peaks sharply after a recent spike and sentiment is low (≤0.4), apply downward correction to prevent overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days after peak) and forecast remains elevated, adjust downward by 3–7% for the next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating 0.3–0.7) and forecast is inconsistent with history, use 3-day moving average of past 18-day history as a baseline.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 70% of forecast’s 1st/2nd day, apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 10–15% for days 10–20.  
- If sentiment history shows a sharp drop (e.g., 0.7 → 0.2) followed by forecast rise, treat as “reversal signal” — reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
